questions.question: Distiguish between Recourse and non recourse factoring.
questions.solution_html:
• Distinguish between Recourse and Non-Recourse Factoring. / [CO4]
  • In recourse factoring, the factor has the right to recover unpaid debts from the client if
  • customers fail to pay. In non -recourse factoring, the factor bears the risk of bad debts and
  • cannot recover losses from the client. Recourse factoring generally involves lower commission
  • charges because the risk is retained by the client. Non -recourse factoring is more expensive
  • due to higher risk assumed by the factor. Thus, the major difference lies in the responsibility
  • for credit risk.

questions.solution_html:
• Explain securitisation of debt. / [CO3]
  • Securitisation of debt is the process of converting illiquid financial assets such as loans and

questions.question: Distiguish between factoring and forfaiting.
questions.solution_html:
• Distinguish between factoring and forfaiting. / [CO4]
  • Factoring mainly deals with short -term receivables arising from domestic trade, whereas
  • forfaiting is used for medium -term and long -term export receivables. In factoring, the factor
  • may or may not assume bad debt risk depending on the agr eement. In forfaiting, the forfaiter
  • usually purchases receivables on a non-recourse basis. Factoring involves continuous financing
  • arrangements, while forfaiting is generally related to a single export transaction. Furthermore,
  • forfaiting is mainly used in international trade finance.

questions.question: Distiguish between Financial system and Financial services.
questions.solution_html:
• Distinguish between Financial System and Financial Services. / [CO1]
  • The financial system refers to the overall framework consisting of financial institutions,
  • markets, instruments, and regulations that facilitate the flow of funds in an economy. Financial
  • services are the specific services provided by financial institutions within the financial system.
  • The financial system provides the structure, whereas financial services provide operational
  • activities like banking, insurance, leasing, and investment management. Financial services are
  • a component of the broader financial system. Thus, the financial system is comprehensive in
  • nature while financial services are functional activities.

questions.question: Describe the objectives and provisions of SARFAESI Act.
questions.solution_html:
• Describe the objectives and provisions of SARFAESI Act. / [CO3]
  • The SARFAESI Act stands for the Securitisation and Reconstruction of Financial Assets and
  • Enforcement of Security Interest Act , 2002. The Act was enacted to help banks and financial
  • institutions recover non-performing assets (NPAs) without the intervention of courts. One of
  • the main objectives of the Act is to strengthen the financial sector by improving the recovery
  • mechanism of defaulted loans. It empowers secured creditors to seize and sell secured assets
  • of borrowers in case of default. The Act also facilitates securitisation and reconstruction of
  • financial assets. Under the Act, Asset Reconstruction Companies (ARCs) can acquire bad loans
  • from banks and manage recovery. The Act provides powers to banks to take possession of
  • collateral securities after giving proper notice to borrowers. Borrowers are generally given 60
  • days’ notice to repay outstanding dues before action is initiated. SARFAESI also allows banks
  • to appoint managers for managing secured assets. The Act improves liquidity and reduces the
  • burden of bad debts on financial institutions. However, agricultural land is excluded from the
  • provisions of the Act. Overall, the SARFAESI Act plays a major role in strengthening credit
  • discipline and improving banking efficiency in India.

questions.question: Analyse the advantages and limitations of leasing in comparison with hire purchase.
questions.solution_html:
• Analyse the advantages and limitations of leasing in comparison with hire purchase.
  • / [CO4]
  • Leasing and hire purchase are two important methods of asset financing used by businesses. In
  • leasing, the ownership of the asset remains with the lessor, whereas in hire purchase ownership
  • is transferred to the hirer after the final payment. One major advantage of leasing is tha t it
  • requires less initial investment compared to hire purchase. Leasing provides flexibility as the
  • lessee can upgrade assets easily after the lease period. Lease rentals are generally treated as
  • business expenses and may provide tax benefits. Leasing also reduces the risk of obsolescence
  • because ownership remains with the lessor. However, leasing does not provide ownership
  • rights to the user of the asset. In hire purchase, the buyer gradually acquires ownership of the
  • asset through installment payments. H ire purchase is beneficial for businesses that want
  • permanent ownership of the asset. However, it usually requires higher down payments and
  • involves higher financial commitment. Leasing may become more expensive in the long run if
  • lease rentals exceed the value of ownership. Therefore, both leasing and hire purchase have
  • distinct advantages and limitations depending on the financial needs and objectives of the
  • business.

questions.question: Explain the functions of merchant banks. / [CO1, CO2] [15x2 = 30]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the functions of merchant banks. / [CO1, CO2]
  • Merchant banks are specialized financial institutions that provide financial advisory and
  • investment services to businesses and governments. One important function of merchant banks
  • is issue management, which includes managing public issues of shares and d ebentures. They
  • assist companies in preparing prospectuses, obtaining regulatory approvals, and marketing
  • securities to investors. Merchant banks also provide underwriting services by guaranteeing the
  • subscription of securities issues. They offer corporate advisory services related to mergers,
  • acquisitions, restructuring, and diversification. Portfolio management services are provided to
  • help investors manage their investments effectively. Merchant banks assist in loan syndication
  • by arranging large loans f rom multiple financial institutions. They also provide project
  • counseling and feasibility studies for new business ventures. Merchant banks help companies
  • in raising foreign capital and managing international financial transactions. Advisory services
  • related to capital structure and investment decisions are another important function. They
  • contribute to the development of capital markets by promoting efficient allocation of financial
  • resources. Thus, merchant banks play a significant role in financial management and industrial
  • growth.
